title: CaddySense

abstract: |
  This thesis presents CaddySense, a hybrid AI-driven golf coaching system that is designed to provide users personalized, interpretable, and accessible golf performance advice for all levels of golfers. Current AI systems in sports are often rely on predictive models to analyze elite-level performance, which can lack transparency and accessibility for recreational golfers who may lack coaches to help with their game. To address this gap, CaddySense puts together structured performance metrics using conversational AI models, which allows for evaluation of driving distance, greens in regulation, putting consistency, and approach shot proximity. This is all done using a locally hosted large language model that is able to generate feedback based on a user's personal skill-level. This evaluation was conducted through controlled environmental conditions, and also used synthetic golfer profiles that show different ranges of skill level and conditions. 
  The results show consistent rule-backed classifications, strong performance in AI-generated feedback using the given metrics, and a reliable level of rules followed that were predetermined. These results help the system to keep transparency when the data given is missing or incomplete. Overall, the findings from this research prove suggest that a hybrid modeled approach when putting together rule-based logic with generative AI can support helpful and correct coaching advice. CaddySense contributes to AI-driven sports analysis that includes user trust, privacy through local storage, and full explain ability. Future work can include real-world experimentation, performance tracking, and more deployment options in order to improve practical impacts of users around the world.
